VDR-CSO-DET.explanation: Daily scanner runs, staffed threat-intelligence and disclosure intake, scheduled testing, and manual control reviews identify technical and process weaknesses.
VDR-CSO-DET.additionalAssurance: A daily reconciliation checks that every detection source reaches our tracking register.

VDR-CSO-RES.explanation: Analysts maintain a daily reviewed register covering ownership, evaluation, exploitation evidence, mitigation, remediation, and reporting for every detected vulnerability.

VDR-CSO-FAV.explanation: Missed scans, review failures, and reporting errors become vulnerability tickets with owners and tracked corrective actions.

VDR-CSO-DFR.explanation: Microsegmentation, restricted administration, and hardened templates contain compromise and keep recovery procedures manageable.

VDR-CSO-ADT.explanation: Legacy scans run automatically, but costly workflow integration leaves evaluation and response tracking manual.
VDR-CSO-ADT.customerRisk: Manual handoffs can delay action on agency-impacting findings.
VDR-CSO-ADT.providerCompensation: Supervisors reconcile scan results and tickets daily.
VDR-CSO-ADT.agencyCompensation: Agencies can review the weekly exception summary and escalate missing actions.

VDR-CSO-DAC.explanation: Legacy deployment tooling lacks automatic detection after changes because integrating representative tests is complex.
VDR-CSO-DAC.customerRisk: Changed resources may expose agencies before the next scheduled scan.
VDR-CSO-DAC.providerCompensation: Operators manually scan changed resources before release and verify isolation.
VDR-CSO-DAC.agencyCompensation: Agencies can request the release test record before enabling affected integrations.

VDR-CSO-MSP.explanation: Credentialed scans use dedicated restricted identities without disabling endpoint protection, firewall controls, or production hardening.

VDR-CSO-AKE.explanation: A release checklist compares images against the current KEV catalog and blocks activation until listed vulnerabilities are removed.

VDR-CSO-SIR.explanation: We scan every resource and do not exercise the optional sampling permission.

VDR-TFR-NMV.explanation: Process owners verify and validate all non-machine resources quarterly and record completed reviews in the register.

VDR-TFR-PDD.explanation: Machine scanning meets the fourteen-day Class C interval, but some legacy configuration and process drift checks remain monthly.
VDR-TFR-PDD.customerRisk: Undetected drift can expose agency workloads between reviews.
VDR-TFR-PDD.providerCompensation: Change approval and microsegmentation reduce unreviewed changes and lateral movement.
VDR-TFR-PDD.agencyCompensation: Agencies can limit integrations and request configuration evidence for important changes.

VDR-TFR-PCD.explanation: Stable machine resources receive monthly scans, but some stable non-machine resources receive only quarterly detection reviews.
VDR-TFR-PCD.customerRisk: Stale procedures or configuration assumptions could persist beyond the Class C monthly target.
VDR-TFR-PCD.providerCompensation: Owners review operational exceptions weekly and investigate reported inconsistencies.
VDR-TFR-PCD.agencyCompensation: Agencies can flag unexpected behavior and request focused reviews.

VDR-TFR-PVR.explanation: We meet the highest-risk Class C impact-reduction intervals but cannot consistently meet every lower-risk interval on tightly coupled legacy components.
VDR-TFR-PVR.completionTargetExplanation: Supplier-dependent upgrades prevent a reliable completion estimate.
VDR-TFR-PVR.customerRisk: Some agency exposures may persist beyond recommended intervals.
VDR-TFR-PVR.providerCompensation: Isolation and targeted filtering reduce exposure while owners track remaining risk.
VDR-TFR-PVR.agencyCompensation: Agencies can restrict affected integrations until verified risk reductions are reported.

VDR-TFR-RMN.explanation: Maintenance meetings assign remaining vulnerabilities for mitigation or remediation based on recorded residual risk.

VDR-TFR-KEV.explanation: The response lead checks the KEV catalog daily and schedules actual remediation by its due dates even when interim mitigations are effective.

VDR-TFR-PSD.explanation: Legacy scanners cover daily high-risk samples, but some isolated machine groups are sampled weekly rather than every three days.
VDR-TFR-PSD.customerRisk: Vulnerabilities in those groups may remain undetected longer than recommended.
VDR-TFR-PSD.providerCompensation: Strict ingress rules and daily host alerts help identify suspicious activity.
VDR-TFR-PSD.agencyCompensation: Agencies can keep connections to those groups disabled unless needed.

VDR-TFR-MVX.explanation: This offering uses Rev5 Class C, so 20x machine verification does not apply; we address VDR-TFR-MVF.

VDR-TFR-MVF.explanation: Administrators verify and validate all machine resources monthly using configuration exports, health checks, and documented manual review.

VER-EVA-ELX.explanation: Analysts manually evaluate exploitation prerequisites against actual system configuration and document the supporting evidence for each finding.

VER-EVA-EIR.explanation: Analysts trace direct and indirect internet payload paths, including application-mediated paths across microsegmented networks.

VER-EVA-EPA.explanation: The response lead assigns N0–N5 ratings using likely effects on each agency and shared-service impacts, retaining the rationale and history.

VER-EVA-AIA.explanation: The evaluation checklist assumes automated exploitation unless documented technical evidence proves otherwise.

VER-EVA-GRV.explanation: We track findings individually because reliable grouping across inconsistent legacy inventories would require costly integration.
VER-EVA-GRV.completionTargetExplanation: Individual tracking will remain our approach for the current platform.
VER-EVA-GRV.customerRisk: Duplicate records can increase workload and delay related responses.
VER-EVA-GRV.providerCompensation: A coordinator reconciles affected components daily and assigns shared owners.
VER-EVA-GRV.agencyCompensation: Agencies can request a consolidated explanation for findings affecting the same service.

VER-EVA-EFP.explanation: Analysts inspect affected versions and reproduce findings where safe before documenting false positives.

VER-EVA-EFA.explanation: Manual assessments cover criticality, reachability, exploitability, and privilege, but documentation of the other contextual factors remains inconsistent.
VER-EVA-EFA.customerRisk: Missing prevalence or vulnerability-interaction evidence may understate agency impact.
VER-EVA-EFA.providerCompensation: Senior analysts review high-impact decisions and known threat intelligence daily.
VER-EVA-EFA.agencyCompensation: Agencies can provide mission context and ask for reassessment of disputed ratings.

VER-RPT-PER.explanation: A daily reconciliation produces controlled updates for all necessary parties covering all new activity, including manual verification and validation.

VER-RPT-VDT.explanation: Analysts populate all applicable VER-RPT-VDT fields, including times, historical ratings, reduction plans, overdue explanations, and disposition, then validate the exported JSON.

VER-RPT-AVI.explanation: A separate register supplies all required accepted-vulnerability fields, including acceptance reasons and practical agency mitigation information.

VER-RPT-NID.explanation: The reporting lead removes exploit-enabling details while providing necessary parties enough evidence for risk-based decisions.

VER-RPT-HLO.explanation: Reports summarize scanning and patching, but consolidating penetration tests and disclosure activity into an overview remains manual and incomplete.
VER-RPT-HLO.customerRisk: Agencies may underestimate activity outside routine scanning.
VER-RPT-HLO.providerCompensation: Detailed underlying records remain available through controlled sharing.
VER-RPT-HLO.agencyCompensation: Agencies can request the separate testing and disclosure summaries.

VER-RPT-RPD.explanation: We exercise the public-disclosure permission only after the security lead determines publication is unlikely to enable exploitation.

VER-TFR-MHR.explanation: All necessary parties receive a consistent human-readable report every month, assembled and checked by two analysts.

VER-TFR-MAV.explanation: The response lead marks a vulnerability accepted immediately when remediation or full mitigation within 192 days is unlikely and reviews elapsed time daily.

VER-TFR-MRH.explanation: Reports are shared securely, but automated retrieval of historical JSON is unavailable because the legacy reporting platform lacks a suitable interface.
VER-TFR-MRH.customerRisk: Agency systems cannot automatically reconcile recent historical activity.
VER-TFR-MRH.providerCompensation: We supply manually exported historical records on request.
VER-TFR-MRH.agencyCompensation: Agencies can reconcile those exports against monthly reports.

VER-TFR-EVU.explanation: Daily triage handles urgent findings, but some routine evaluations take seven days rather than the Class C five-day target.
VER-TFR-EVU.customerRisk: Delayed contextual evaluation may postpone agency risk decisions.
VER-TFR-EVU.providerCompensation: The duty analyst escalates suspected high-impact exposures immediately.
VER-TFR-EVU.agencyCompensation: Agencies can flag critical dependencies for expedited evaluation.

VER-TFR-IRI.explanation: Incident procedures cover confirmed exploitation, but qualifying internet-reachable likely exploitable findings do not consistently enter incident handling before exploitation.
VER-TFR-IRI.customerRisk: Agencies may receive incident-level coordination later than recommended.
VER-TFR-IRI.providerCompensation: The duty lead sends urgent risk notices and isolates affected components.
VER-TFR-IRI.agencyCompensation: Agencies can trigger their own incident review when notified of these exposures.

VER-TFR-NRI.explanation: For the Class C optional incident classification, we escalate non-internet-reachable likely exploitable N5 findings until verified reduction to N4 or below.
